extracted.intended_audience: readers and practitioners of literary/historical narrative (18th-century novel readers; creative writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and narrator reflections on composing a rhapsodical or digressive history/novel — what materials to gather, how to present documents, pacing of publication, and how to handle inevitable deviations and asides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components to include when writing a history
rubrics_metrics.description: “Accounts to reconcile: Anecdotes to pick up: Inscriptions to make out: Stories to weave in: Traditions to sift: Personages to call upon: Panegyricks to paste up at this door; Pasquinades at that:”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a near-exhaustive list of the incidental materials a historiographer (or writer of a history/ life) will encounter and ought to gather and weigh into the work. Surrounding explanation: the author observes that a man who sits down to write a history cannot go straight; he will be continually detained by these items and must incorporate them into the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate archival interruptions and genealogical detours
rubrics_metrics.description: “There are archives at every stage to be look'd into, and rolls, records, documents, and endless genealogies, which justice ever and anon calls him back to stay the reading of:——In short there is no end of it;”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice about process: writers should expect and allow time for research interruptions (records, rolls, genealogies) and accept that such detours are an intrinsic part of composing history/narrative rather than mere distractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use primary documents verbatim when they are more precise than paraphrase
rubrics_metrics.description: “The article in my mother’s marriage-settlement ... is so much more fully express'd in the deed itself, than ever I can pretend to do it, that it would be barbarity to take it out of the lawyer's hand:—It is as follows.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline to incorporate original texts (indentures, deeds, settlements) in full when they convey meaning more precisely than a summary; the narrator elects to present the deed verbatim rather than paraphrase it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplement the narrative with maps, scholia, illustrations and keys
rubrics_metrics.description: “...a map, now in the hands of the engraver, which, with many other pieces and developements of this work, will be added to the end of the twentieth volume,—not to swell the work,—but by way of commentary, scholium, illustration, and key to such passages, incidents, or innuendos as shall be thought to be either of private interpretation, or of dark or doubtful meaning...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to provide supporting materials (maps, commentaries, scholia, illustrations, keys) to clarify passages, incidents, or innuendos that might be obscure or open to private interpretation — especially useful for complex, digressive works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not hurry—adopt a deliberate, periodic publication pace
rubrics_metrics.description: “These unforeseen stoppages ... have struck out a hint which I am resolved to follow;——and that is,—not to be in a hurry;—but to go on leisurely, writing and publishing two volumes of my life every year;——which, if I am suffered to go on quietly, and can make a tolerable bargain with my bookseller, I shall continue to do as long as I live.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A policy for pacing composition and publication: accept unforeseeable delays, work leisurely, and set a sustainable serial publication cadence (example given: two volumes per year), contingent on practical arrangements with a publisher.
